## Review

**7 out of 10, Effective.** Presentation quality, judged with the SlideDeck Co review heuristic (https://slidedeck.co/review-methodology/). The ask, the evidence and the merit of the idea are not rated.

The deck is competent and usable for a read-at-desk investor audience. A six-part section navigation bar with colour-coded tabs, divider photos and a table of contents give a clear route, and context arrives before it is needed: the fact sheet on slide 5, then results (8), outlook (9) and acquisitions (13-16). Weaknesses are consequential: most content slides use titles that name a topic rather than a conclusion (6, 7, 10, 26, 28), tiny footnotes and dense text on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41 are hard to read, and the last 25 pages are reconciliation tables and legal text that cannot be read as a presentation. Slide 22 shows the chart problems: bars without a clear message, a pie chart with no labels on the slices, and a lot of empty space.

**Worth keeping:** Keep the colour-coded section tab bar, the full-bleed photo dividers, the big-number stat blocks on slides 8, 14 and 17, and the scannable fact sheet on slide 5.

**Most useful repair:** Replace the topic titles with conclusion titles, enlarge or cut the text and chart labels on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41, and label the pie slices directly on slide 22.

**What would change the score:** I would move the appendix reconciliations to a separate document, keeping only a short set of key tables, and split the dense timeline and ESG pages into fewer, larger-type slides.

_Confidence high. 69 of 69 pages inspected on contact sheets, 4 at readable size. Reviewed Reviewed 2026-11-08. Model-assisted review (claude-sonnet-5-5)._

## Summary

The deck opens with a title slide reading Investor Presentation, dated November 2026, followed by forward-looking statement and non-GAAP disclaimers and a table of contents. Its main sections run in order: Company Overview, Recent Highlights, Portfolio Update, Growth Opportunities, Corporate Responsibility, and Reconciliations and Supplemental Information. The company overview uses a fact sheet with pie charts for brand, chain scale, manager and business mix, a top-10 markets list, and a comparison against other full-service lodging REITs. Recent highlights cover Q3 2026 results, a full-year 2026 outlook table, and acquisition slides for two hotels, each with a rationale list and a property overview. The portfolio update covers rate-driven revenue growth, group and transient demand, and a capital allocation summary. Growth opportunities detail renovation programs with Marriott and Hyatt and a capex summary table. Corporate responsibility closes the main body with climate, sustainability and governance pages. Slides 5, 9 and 22 are good models for dense data layout, and slides 18 and 28 for tabular comparisons.

## Questions about this deck

**How many slides does the Host Hotels & Resorts investor presentation have?**

The deck has 69 pages. Slide 3 is the table of contents, which lists its main sections: Company Overview, Recent Highlights, Portfolio Update, Growth Opportunities, Corporate Responsibility, and Reconciliations & Supplemental Information.

**What does the Host Hotels & Resorts deck say about its full year 2026 outlook?**

Slide 9 gives a Full Year 2026 estimate of $392 for Comparable Hotel Total RevPAR, up 6.0% versus 2025, and $1,865 million for Adjusted EBITDAre, up 6.1%. The same slide estimates NAREIT FFO per diluted share at $2.17, up 6.9%.

**What does the Host Hotels & Resorts deck say about its liquidity and credit rating?**

Slide 8 reports $2.6 billion in total available liquidity and 2.3x net leverage as adjusted as of September 30, 2026. Slide 11 says the company is investment grade rated and is the only investment grade rated lodging REIT.

**What does the Host Hotels & Resorts deck say about the 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge acquisition?**

Slide 13 lists a $202 million purchase price, which reflects an acquisition multiple of 10.2x based on 2026E EBITDA. Slide 14 describes the property as having 195 keys including 29 suites.

**Layout**

Full-height photograph occupies the left 61.5% of the slide below a six-tab navigation strip spanning the full width across the top. The right side is a white panel holding the Host Hotels & Resorts logo centred above the title 'Company Overview', which sits in the vertical middle-upper area. A dark translucent caption band runs along the bottom edge, with the caption at the left margin. No slide number or footer is visible.

**Visuals**

Photograph of a hotel lobby, the Ritz-Carlton Naples, Tiburón. Subject: a large round cream-upholstered sofa with cushions in the foreground on a pale stone floor, potted palms and tropical plants around it, a pair of large ring-shaped pendant chandeliers with warm amber-lit alabaster rings, columns, a dark wood and patterned screen, a marble side table at lower left, and a glimpse of a reception desk at left. Composition: wide interior view from a low angle, framed to the left 61.5% of the slide, not cropped into a shape, shown as a rectangle that runs from the top navigation strip to the bottom band. Lighting: warm, soft ambient interior light with amber highlights. Dominant colours: beige, cream, sand, warm brown, and green foliage. No overlay on the photograph itself. Logo: Host Hotels & Resorts logo at upper centre of the right panel, consisting of a stylised gold and navy geometric mark above the word HOST in navy serif capitals and the words HOTELS & RESORTS beneath in smaller navy serif capitals with a registered mark.

### Slide 5

**Review notes**

- Worth studying: A single fact sheet combines several pie charts, a ranked top-10 markets list and a headline stat row, so a dense set of numbers stays readable on one page.
- Review: A six-part section navigation bar with colour-coded tabs, divider photos and a table of contents give a clear route, and context arrives before it is needed: the fact sheet on slide 5, then results (8), outlook (9) and acquisitions (13-16).
- Worth keeping: Keep the colour-coded section tab bar, the full-bleed photo dividers, the big-number stat blocks on slides 8, 14 and 17, and the scannable fact sheet on slide 5.

**Layout**

Full-width six-tab navigation strip across the top edge (tab 1 highlighted); the slide title sits left-aligned below it at about 8% from the left margin. Below the title, a four-column key-figure row, a horizontal rule, and a three-column benefit row sit on white; a full-width light blue-grey panel holds a left column (headline figures and ranked Top-10 list) and a 2x2 grid of labelled 100% bar charts, followed by four numbered footnotes, a copyright line at bottom left and the page number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Four bar-style 100% composition charts plus one ranked list, all printed with values; no photographs or logos. (a) MANAGER (room count): one vertical stacked bar with segments BRAND MANAGED 89% (top, dark navy) and INDEPENDENT 11% (bottom, royal blue); labels sit to the right of each segment. (b) CHAIN SCALE (room count): one vertical stacked bar with segments UPPER UPSCALE 71% (top, navy), LUXURY 26% (royal blue), UPSCALE 2% (light blue), MIDSCALE 1% (yellow), labels to the right. (c) BRANDS (2025 Hotel Revenue): one vertical stacked bar with segments MARRIOTT 67% (navy), HYATT 18% (royal blue), 1 HOTEL 6% (maroon), ACCOR 4% (yellow), HILTON 4% (purple), OTHER/INDEPENDENT 1% (green), labels to the right. (d) BUSINESS MIX (2025 Room Revenues): one vertical stacked bar with segments GROUP 34% (navy), TRANSIENT 61% (light blue), CONTRACT 5% (yellow). Bar width is about 4% of slide width each; no axes, gridlines or legend; segment heights proportional to the printed percentages. Top-10 Markets (2025 Total Revenue): a numbered list of ten markets with percentages right-aligned in a second column: 1 New York 9%, 2 San Diego 9%, 3 Florida Gulf Coast 8%, 4 Maui 7%, 5 San Francisco/San Jose 7%, 6 Phoenix 7%, 7 Orlando 5%, 8 Washington, DC (CBD) 5%, 9 Miami 5%, 10 O’ahu 4%. KPI figures are plain typography: HST NASDAQ; S&P 500 SINCE 2007; $15.6B equity market cap; $19.6B enterprise value; 1st became lodging REIT in 1998; #1 total shareholder returns; INVESTMENT GRADE SINCE 2013; 77 hotels; 41,800 rooms. Thin grey vertical dividers separate the KPI columns and benefit columns, and a thin grey horizontal rule runs across the full width beneath the KPIs.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF with a light blue-grey #EBEFF9 panel behind the lower body (y 41% to 86.4%). White background with a light blue-grey panel (#EBEFF9) across the lower body. Title in Quicksand Light, black #000000, about 4.1% of slide height, sentence-case. Headline figures in Source Sans Pro Black, royal blue #0F3DA2, about 5.9% of slide height. Sub-labels in Source Sans Pro SemiBold uppercase light blue #5DA6E0 at about 3.0%. Body and footnote text in Source Sans Pro Light, navy #172645 or dark grey #313335, about 1.8% to 2.0% of slide height (footnotes 1.2%). Section headings in Source Sans Pro SemiBold navy #172645 at about 2.2%. Navigation tabs use Quicksand Medium uppercase white text at 1.67% on grey #AFAFAC tabs with the active tab in royal blue #0F3DA2. Flat design: no gradients, shadows or rounded corners; bars are square-cornered solid fills with white bold percentages; thin grey dividers (#A0A0A0, about 1 pt).

### Slide 6

**Text**

Leading Bottom-Line Growth / Entering the pandemic with a fortress balance sheet allowed Host to opportunistically re-invest in our portfolio and accretively recycle assets. As a result, full year 2025 Adjusted EBITDAre and Nareit FFO/share grew meaningfully above 2019 levels while other full-service lodging REITs lagged. / 2025 VS 2019 ADJUSTED EBITDARE GROWTH(1) / 13% / -17% / Host / Other Full-Service Lodging REIT Avg. / 2025 VS 2019 NAREIT FFO PER SHARE GROWTH(1) / 19% / -33% / Host / Other Full-Service Lodging REIT Avg. / 2025 VS 2019 TOTAL DIVIDENDS PER SHARE GROWTH(2) / 12% / -55% / Host / Other Full-Service Lodging REIT Avg. / TOTAL SHAREHOLDER RETURN 12/31/18 – 12/31/2025(2,3) / 37% / -23% / Host / Other Full-Service Lodging REIT Avg. / 1) Adjusted EBITDAre and FFO/share are non-GAAP financial measures. Host’s 2025 net income growth and diluted earnings per share growth compared to 2019 are (17)% and (13)% , respectively. See Reconciliations & Supplemental Information for reconciliation of comparable GAAP measures. Other Full-Service Lodging REITs (listed on slide 5) calculate Adjusted EBITDAre differently and this presentation does not account for those differences. / 2) Source: Factset. / 3) See footnote 2 on slide 5. The returns are based on historical results and are not intended to suggest future performance. / © Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. / 6 / COMPANY OVERVIEW / RECENT HIGHLIGHTS / PORTFOLIO UPDATE / GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES / CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY / RECONCILIATIONS & SUPPLEMENTAL INFO

**Layout**

Six equal-width navigation tabs run across the top edge, flush to the top and sides, each 4.7% of slide height tall with the first tab active. The title sits left-aligned at about 8% from the left edge, followed by a two-line intro paragraph. Below it a 2x2 grid of four diverging bar charts is split by a thin vertical divider at about 50% width and a thin horizontal divider at about 57% height. Footnotes sit left-aligned at about 7% from the left, with the copyright line at the bottom left and the page number at the bottom right.

**Visuals**

Four diverging bar charts, each showing a baseline with one blue bar above it for Host and one dark navy bar below it for the Other Full-Service Lodging REIT average. Top-left: title 2025 VS 2019 ADJUSTED EBITDARE GROWTH(1); Host bar labelled 13% (about 13 percent above baseline, about 4.8% of slide height tall); Other REIT bar labelled -17% (about 17 percent below baseline, about 5.9% of slide height tall); baseline is light grey, x 8.2 to 42.6, y 39.9. Top-right: title 2025 VS 2019 NAREIT FFO PER SHARE GROWTH(1); Host bar 19% (about 19 percent above baseline, about 4.0% tall); Other REIT bar -33% (about 33 percent below baseline, about 6.3% tall); baseline x 55.0 to 89.4, y 39.5. Bottom-left: title 2025 VS 2019 TOTAL DIVIDENDS PER SHARE GROWTH(2); Host bar 12% (about 12 percent above baseline, about 1.9% tall); Other REIT bar -55% (about 55 percent below baseline, about 9.0% tall); baseline x 10.0 to 44.4, y 70.0. Bottom-right: title TOTAL SHAREHOLDER RETURN 12/31/18 – 12/31/2025(2,3); Host bar 37% (about 37 percent above baseline, about 4.9% tall); Other REIT bar -23% (about 23 percent below baseline, about 3.0% tall); baseline x 55.0 to 89.4, y 74.7. Category labels under each pair: Host and Other Full-Service Lodging REIT Avg. No legend. No highlighted points beyond the blue Host bars. Bars are flat rectangles with no gradient, outline or shadow.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white corporate look. Navigation tabs use Quicksand Medium uppercase white text on grey #AFAFAC tabs with the active tab in blue #0F3DA2. Title in Quicksand Light, black #000000, about 4.1% of slide height. Intro paragraph in Source Sans Pro Light, #292929, about 2.6% of slide height. Chart headings in Source Sans Pro Black uppercase, #292929, about 2.6% of slide height, with superscript footnote markers. Value labels in Source Sans Pro Black, #404040, about 1.8%. Category labels in Source Sans Pro Light, #595959, about 1.7%. Footnotes in Source Sans Pro Light, #000000, about 1.2%. Page number in Source Sans Pro Light, #898989. Bars: Host #0F3DA2 blue, peers #172645 navy. Dividers and baselines are light grey hairlines. No corner radii, shadows or gradients.

### Slide 7

**Text**

COMPANY / OVERVIEW / RECENT / HIGHLIGHTS / PORTFOLIO / UPDATE / GROWTH / OPPORTUNITIES / CORPORATE / RESPONSIBILITY / RECONCILIATIONS & / SUPPLEMENTAL INFO / Shareholder Value Creation / Host leads the full-service lodging REITs in cumulative free cash flow from 2019 through 2025 despite proactively accelerating capex investment during the pandemic. / In addition to portfolio reinvestment, we elevated the quality of the portfolio through accretive portfolio recycling which has led to a meaningful increase in Adjusted EBITDAre per key while reducing key count. / FREE CASH FLOW AS % OF TOTAL REVENUE(1) / (Cumulative from 2019-2025) / 10.2% / HST / Other Full-Service Lodging REIT Avg. / 4.9% / ADJUSTED EBITDARE PER KEY(2) / +26% / Increase in Adjusted EBITDAre per key from 2019 to 2025, representing a meaningful increase in portfolio quality as key count decreased (9)% through accretive portfolio recycling. / 1) / Free Cash Flow as a percentage of total revenue is a non-GAAP financial measure. The comparable metric using GAAP amounts is net cash provided by (used in) operating activities as a percentage of total revenues. Our net cash provided by operating activities as a percentage of total revenues from 2019 – 2025 was 22.2%. The other full-service lodging REIT average is based on their annual filings. See Reconciliations & Supplemental Information for how we calculate free cash flow and reconciliations to the comparable GAAP measure. See footnote 2 on slide 5 for a listing of full-service lodging REITs used in the comparison. / 2) / Adjusted EBITDAre per key is a non-GAAP financial measure. Host's 2025 net income per key change compared to 2019 is a decline of (9)%. See Reconciliations & Supplemental Information for reconciliation of comparable GAAP measures. / © 2026 Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. / . / 7

**Layout**

Six-tab section navigation bar runs across the full top edge, with the first tab highlighted in blue and the other five in grey. The title 2026 Outlook sits top-left below the bar at about 8% left margin, followed by the OPERATIONAL OUTLOOK heading and italic subtitle, a centred full-year table in the upper half, and a two-column lower section: left column COMPARABLE RevPAR vs. 2025 with Growth Assumptions and bullets, right column ANNUAL ASSUMPTIONS with three icon-led items. A footnote sits near the bottom, with the copyright line bottom-left and the page number bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Table: Full Year 2026(1) table with three columns, Full Year 2026 label (x 24.5 to 52.7%), Estimate (52.7 to 64.4%), vs. 2025 (64.5 to 75.5%). Header row in #0F3DA2 with white bold text. Seven data rows, each about 3.8% of slide height, in alternating fills #CCCDCF and #E7E8E9, starting with #CCCDCF. Row values: Comparable Hotel Total RevPAR $392 +6.0%; Comparable Hotel RevPAR $237 +6.75%; Comparable Hotel EBITDA Margin 30.0% +80 bps; Comparable Hotel EBITDA (millions) $1,757 +9.1%; Adjusted EBITDAre (in millions) $1,865 +6.1%; NAREIT FFO per diluted share $2.17 +6.9%; Adjusted FFO per diluted share $2.21 +6.8%. Estimate column right-aligned; vs. 2025 column right-aligned. White cell gutters of about 0.3% of slide width. Icons: a blue outline office building (about x 61.3, y 64.2, w 3.0, h 5.5) beside Corporate & Other Expenses; a blue outline stopwatch with a blue circular percent badge (about x 61.3, y 72.7, w 3.6, h 4.3) beside Interest Expense; a blue outline traffic cone on a diamond-shaped base (about x 61.4, y 81.0, w 3.3, h 5.3) beside Capital Expenditures. Icons are line art in #0F3DA2 stroke about 0.2% width, unfilled. No photographs, charts or logos.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, full bleed. Plain white background with no gradient or texture. Titles in near-black #292929; the 2026 Outlook title is Quicksand Light in #000000. Section headings are Source Sans Pro Black, uppercase, letter-spaced, #292929. Body and bullet text in grey #595959. Accent colour is royal blue #0F3DA2 for the active tab, table header and sub-headings. Bullets are #5DA6E0 right-pointing triangles. Nav tabs are #AFAFAC grey with white uppercase Quicksand Medium text. Typefaces are sans-serif throughout. Title about 4.1% of slide height; section headings about 3.3%; body about 2.0 to 2.6%; footnote about 1.2%. Shapes are square-cornered, with no shadows or gradients.

1) Disposition multiples are calculated as the ratio between the sales price (plus estimated avoided capital expenditures over the five years following the disposition dates) and EBITDA on a TTM basis from the disposition date, except
for 2020 – 2022 dispositions which use 2019 full year results as the TTM are not representative of normalized operations. For 2018 –2026 dispositions, combined estimated avoided capital expenditures over the five years following
the disposition dates totaled $1.2 billion. The disposition net income multiple is 29x. For 2021 – 2026 dispositions, combined estimated avoided capital expenditures over the five years following the disposition dates totaled $710
million and the disposition net income multiple is 28x. Acquisition multiples are based on forecast operations in the year of acquisition or, for hotels acquired in 2021, 2019 operations, with the following exceptions: Baker's Cay
Resort Key Largo (2021 acquisition), based on 2021 forecast operations at acquisition, as the property was under renovation and closed for part of 2019; The Laura Hotel (2021 acquisition), based on estimated normalized results at
acquisition that assume results are in-line with the 2019 results of comparable Houston properties, as the property was re-opened with a new manager and brand when acquired in 2021; Alila Ventana Big Sur (2021 acquisition),
based on 2021 forecast operations at acquisition as the property was under renovation for part of 2019; The Alida, Savannah (2021 acquisition), which adjusts 2019 results for construction disruption to the surrounding Plant
Riverside District and for initial ramp-up of hotel operations. Acquisition EBITDA includes an upward adjustment of $13 million to reflect normalized operations for both The Laura Hotel and The Alida, Savannah. The 2018 –2026
acquisition net income multiple is 23x. The 2021 – 2026 acquisition net income multiple is 22x. See Reconciliations and Supplemental Information for reconciliations.
2) A securities rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold securities and may be subject to revision or withdrawal at any time. Credit ratings are subject to change depending on financial and other factors.
3) No market accounts for more than 11% of 2025 hotel net income. See Reconciliations & Supplemental Information for reconciliations of net income to EBITDA.

**Layout**

Full-bleed layout: a six-tab navigation bar runs across the top edge, the slide title Investment Thesis sits top-left at about 8% from the left, below it a left column (Capital Allocation Track Record, EBITDA multiples table, Diverse Portfolio) and a right column starting at about 56% (Strong Balance Sheet, Size, Scale & Reputation) with bulleted text. A full-width photograph fills the lower half from about 38% to 80% of the height, with the footnote block and copyright line below it and the page number bottom-right at about 96%. Left margin about 8%, right margin about 5%.

**Visuals**

One photograph: an aerial dusk view of The Westin Kierland Resort & Spa, a large tan and brown multi-storey hotel with a terracotta tiled roof in the centre, low-rise wings and cabanas to the left, a rectangular turquoise swimming pool with lounge chairs in the lower centre surrounded by rows of tall palm trees, a golf course with green fairways at left, and a distant skyline of mid-rise apartment and office buildings with mountains on the horizon. Warm golden-hour light, dominant colours tan, ochre, green and muted blue; the photo is full-bleed across the slide width, not boxed, and is faded to white at its top edge by a translucent white haze. One data table: navy boxed table with column headers DISPOSITIONS and ACQUISITIONS and row labels 2018 – 2026 and 2021 –2026; cells: 2018 – 2026 dispositions $6.4B @ 16.9x, acquisitions $5.3B @ 13.4x; 2021 –2026 dispositions $2.9B @ 16.5x, acquisitions $3.7B @ 13.0x. Table has a soft drop shadow. Blue ► bullet markers used for lists.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, with the photograph and a white haze overlay across its top edge in the lower half. White background #FFFFFF. Tab bar: six equal grey tabs #AFAFAC with white uppercase Quicksand Medium labels, active tab COMPANY OVERVIEW filled #0F3DA2. Title Investment Thesis in Quicksand Light, black #000000, about 4.1% of slide height. Section headings in Source Sans Pro Regular, blue #2F5597, about 2.8% of slide height. Body text in Source Sans Pro Regular, grey #595959, about 1.8% of slide height. Table numbers in Source Sans Pro Black, white #FFFFFF, about 2.6%; table column headers white-blue #DFEDF9 in Source Sans Regular about 1.5%. Table cells navy #172645 with thin lighter dividers. Bullet arrows ► in ArialMT blue #0F3DA2. Footnotes Source Sans Pro Light black about 1.2% of slide height. Page number Source Sans Pro Light grey #898989. Photo caption white Source Sans Pro Regular. Table has a soft shadow; no rounded corners; no gradients beyond the photo haze.

11

**Layout**

Full-width white slide with a six-tab navigation bar across the top edge (first tab 'COMPANY OVERVIEW' in blue, the other five in grey, each about 16.6% wide, 4.7% tall, touching). Title 'Balance Sheet' is left-aligned at x 7.9%, y 8.6%, with a one-line subtitle beneath at y 16.5%. Three equal navy cards sit in one row at x 7.9%, 36.5% and 65.2% (each 27.9% wide, y 22% to 50%) with gaps of about 0.7%. Below them a section heading and a bar chart occupy the lower half, with a legend at top right of the chart; footnotes sit at y 86.9% to 93.0%, the copyright line bottom-left at y 96.2% and page number bottom-right at x 95.3%, y 96.1%. Left margin about 7.9%, right margin about 6.7%.

**Visuals**

Chart: stacked column chart titled 'MATURITY SCHEDULE ($ in millions)' with superscript (3). Category axis (x) shows 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, 2030, 2031, Thereafter, with a thin light grey baseline (#D9D9D9) from about x 5.7% to 93.0% at y 83.1%. No value axis is printed; bars are drawn to a common linear scale. Series: Senior Notes (blue #0F3DA2): 2026 no bar; 2027 none; 2028 $400; 2029 $650; 2030 $750; 2031 $450; Thereafter $1,800. Term Loan (purple #7567BD): 2031 $500 stacked above Senior Notes; Thereafter $500 stacked above Senior Notes. Mortgage and Other Debt (amber about #F5B400): 2027 $90 bar, with its label printed above the bar in dark grey #404040. Bar tops: 2027 at about 82.2%; 2028 about 79.3%; 2029 about 77.0%; 2030 about 76.1%; 2031 about 74.2% (purple top) and 78.9% (blue top); Thereafter 61.7% (purple top) and 66.3% (blue top). Bar widths about 7.3% each, centred on category labels. Value labels are white inside blue and purple bars and dark inside amber. Legend top right: blue square then 'Senior Notes', purple square then 'Term Loan (3)', amber square then 'Mortgage and Other Debt (4)'. Highlighted points: none. Three navy rectangular KPI cards: (a) TOTAL AVAILABLE LIQUIDITY with large $2.6B figure; (b) INVESTMENT GRADE RATED table with 3 columns AGENCY, RATING, OUTLOOK and 3 rows: Moody’s / Baa2 / Stable; S&P / BBB- / Stable; Fitch / BBB / Stable; (c) UNENCUMBERED with large 99% figure. No photographs, logos or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Plain white background with no gradient, texture or imagery. Title 'Balance Sheet' in Quicksand Light, black #000000, about 4.07% of slide height, sentence case. Subtitle in Source Sans Pro Light, #292929, about 2.60%, with bold words 'flexibility' and 'optionality' in Source Sans Pro SemiBold. Navigation tabs in Quicksand Medium uppercase white #FFFFFF at about 1.67%, centred, active tab fill #0F3DA2, inactive tabs fill #AFAFAC. Navy cards #172645 with square corners, no border, no shadow; card headings Source Sans Pro SemiBold white #FFFFFF about 2.60%; hero numbers Source Sans Pro Black #BEDBF3 about 10.00%; card body text Source Sans Pro Light white about 1.96%; table column headings SemiBold white about 2.04%, values Light white about 2.04%; note line 'Only investment grade rated lodging REIT' Light #BEDBF3 about 2.04%. Section heading 'MATURITY SCHEDULE' Source Sans Pro SemiBold #0F3DA2 about 2.60%. Accent blue #0F3DA2, purple #7567BD, amber #F5B400. Body text grey #595959 for legend and callout. Footnotes Source Sans Pro Light black about 1.20%. Lines and shapes: flat fills, no rounded corners, no shadows, no gradients; chart baseline thin light grey; callout left bar is a 0.3% wide dark grey #595959 vertical rule.

The bridge's stone tower and suspension cables run across the centre-right; a tall dark glass tower stands left of the bridge; the Manhattan skyline with lit windows is at far left. Foreground: a glass balustrade with a brushed metal top rail on the left; beige cushioned teak sofas with grey and blue-grey throw pillows; a teak coffee table holding a small copper-finished table lamp and a potted plant; a grey-blue cushion in the lower foreground; brick paving; a green tree and planters at the right. A pier with dark piles and a floating dock sits on the water at left. Lighting: twilight sky graded from deep blue-violet at top to orange-pink at the horizon, with warm lamplight on the furniture. Dominant colours: blue #3B4A7A, violet #6B5E8E, orange #E9A46A, warm wood #A0643A, grey-beige #C9C2B5. Framing: wide landscape view cropped at the right edge of the panel, bleeds off the top, left and bottom edges of the slide, with no border. Overlay: the navy band at 80% opacity covers the bottom of the photo. Logo (white panel): Host Hotels & Resorts mark, a two-part chevron-like symbol with a gold-khaki left half #B09A5E and a navy right half #172645 above the word HOST in navy serif capitals and HOTELS & RESORTS® in smaller navy serif capitals beneath. **Layout**

Six equal-width grey tabs run across the full top edge as a navigation bar, with the second tab RECENT HIGHLIGHTS filled teal to mark the active section. The title block sits in a left text column starting at about 8% from the left edge, with the title at about 9% from the top and the subtitle beneath it. Bullets are left-aligned in one column from about 11% to 56% of the width. Three photographs are stacked in a full-height right column from about 64% to 100% of the width, butted together with no gaps. A footnote sits at the bottom of the left column with the copyright line below it, and the page number sits at the bottom right of the left area, just left of the photo column.

**Visuals**

Three photographs stacked in the right column, top to bottom. (1) Exterior entrance of the hotel: a row of tall vertical wooden slats runs across the upper facade behind glass doors, with a rusted corten-style steel panel on the right carrying a large dark numeral 1 above the word HOTEL and the script words brooklyn bridge; in front are potted shrubs and grey stone pavers, with white gravel and small uplights along the base; daylight, neutral and warm, with a cool grey-green tone; full-bleed to the right edge and cropped at the top by the nav bar. (2) Guest room interior: floor-to-ceiling windows on the left show a city skyline and the Brooklyn Bridge at right; a grey hammock hangs in front of the windows, a pair of grey knitted poufs sit on dark wood flooring with a patterned rug, and a made bed with grey throw is on the right; warm wood and grey tones with a daylight palette; full-bleed, rectangular, no overlay. (3) Lobby lounge: a wood-slat ceiling with recessed ceiling lights, grey upholstered sofas with cushions in the foreground, white and grey armchairs, a round side table, woven stools, potted plants, and a pale wood reception desk visible in the distance; neutral greys, beige and warm wood, soft daylight from large windows at the back; full-bleed, rectangular, no overlay. No charts, tables, logos or icons. A small teal gradient chevron arrow at the left edge is a graphic accent.

**Layout**

A grey six-tab navigation bar runs across the top edge (0 to 4.7% of height), with the second tab 'Recent Highlights' filled teal. The title sits left-aligned at about 7.9% from the left edge, below the bar. Three text columns start at x about 7.8%, 38.9% and 69.9%, with headings aligned at the same baseline band. A teal banner with three large figures is centred over the lower edge of the text and the top of a full-width three-photo row (y 52.3% to 87.1%), which runs edge to edge with no margins or gutters. Footnotes and the copyright line sit bottom-left at about 6.9% from the left, and the page number sits bottom-right at x 95.3%, y 96.1%.

**Visuals**

Three photographs in a full-bleed row: (1) left, rooftop infinity pool with turquoise water, teal tiled edge, wooden deck, row of lounge chairs with folded towels, a dark parasol, and a Manhattan skyline across a river under a pale blue sky with thin clouds; daylight; blue, teal and green dominant; rectangular, not cropped to a shape. (2) centre, lounge interior with a floor-to-ceiling living wall of climbing green plants on a concrete wall, tan leather sofas, a wooden low table, woven straw stools and potted plants, tall windows at right; warm interior light; green, brown and grey dominant. (3) right, restaurant dining room with tan upholstered wooden chairs, tables set with glassware, a back bar with rows of bottles, pendant lights, large windows showing green trees, and potted plants; warm amber light; tan, brown and green dominant. A teal banner (see elements) overlaps the top edges of photos 1 to 3. No logos or charts.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background with grey (#AFAFAC) navigation tabs and one teal (#407676) active tab. Title is black (#000000) in a light geometric sans (Quicksand Light), about 4.1% of slide height. Section headings are teal #407676 in a semibold humanist sans (Source Sans Pro SemiBold) at about 3.3%. Body text is dark grey #292929 in Source Sans Pro Regular at about 2.0%, with teal #407676 triangular bullets and teal dashes for sub-bullets. Navigation labels are white Quicksand Medium in capitals at about 1.7% with wide letter spacing. Banner figures are white Source Sans Pro Black at about 5.2%; captions are white Source Sans Pro Regular at about 2.0%. Banner is a flat teal rectangle with a faint drop shadow and square corners. Photos have square corners, no border.

15

**Layout**

Two-column layout on a white field: a narrow text column occupies the left roughly 64% of the width and a stacked three-photo column fills the right 36% full-bleed to the slide edge. A row of six equal-width navigation tabs runs across the top band (about 4.7% of height), with the second tab, RECENT HIGHLIGHTS, highlighted in teal. The title sits left-aligned at about 7.9% from the left edge beneath the tabs, with the subtitle beneath it; the nine bullets are left-aligned in a single column below. Footnotes sit bottom-left above the copyright line, and the slide number sits bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Three photographs stacked in the right column, each full-bleed to the right slide edge and abutting each other with no gaps or borders. Top photo (x64.0 y4.2 w36.0 h33.5): exterior of a roughly ten-storey hotel with a blue reflective glass curtain wall, white cumulus clouds in a blue sky, a red-flowering crape myrtle tree at the left edge, green street trees and a parking area in the foreground, and a rooftop sign reading RENAISSANCE with a stylised R logo at the top right of the building; bright daylight, building shown from a low three-quarter angle, cropped at the top by the tab band. Middle photo (x64.0 y36.0 w36.0 h30.9): guest room with a king bed dressed in a white duvet and a charcoal-grey throw across the foot, dark brown upholstered headboard panel, a cylindrical wall pendant lamp at right, a red armchair and dark wood desk at left, sheer white curtains and dark drapes around a window; warm lamplight and neutral cream, charcoal and brown tones. Bottom photo (x64.0 y66.7 w36.0 h33.3): restaurant interior with long rows of wooden tables and wooden chairs with red seat pads, many gold metal birdcage-style pendant lights hanging from the ceiling, a dark red curtain at the right, a mosaic wall of round tiles in grey, purple and white, and a grey floor; warm, low lighting in browns, gold and red. No charts, tables, logos or icons other than the teal chevron at the left margin, which is a decorative shape and not a logo.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white background with a six-tab grey navigation band across the top. Grey tabs #AFAFAC with white Quicksand Medium capitals; the active RECENT HIGHLIGHTS tab is teal #407676. Title is black #000000 in Quicksand Light, about 3.7% of slide height, sentence case. Subtitle ACQUISITION RATIONALE is dark teal #203B3B in Source Sans Pro SemiBold capitals at about 3.0% height. Bullet text is #292929 in Source Sans Pro Light at about 2.2% height, with teal #407676 triangular bullet markers. Footnotes and copyright are black #000000 Source Sans Pro Light at about 1.2% height; the slide number is grey #898989. Accent colour teal #407676. Shapes are square-cornered with no shadows or gradients except the teal-to-white gradient chevron at the left margin, which fades from teal at its right point toward pale grey-white at its left edge. Photos are rectangular with no borders.

**Layout**

Six equal-width grey navigation tabs run across the top edge of the slide, flush with the top and sides, with the second tab (RECENT HIGHLIGHTS) filled teal. Below them the title sits left-aligned at about 8% from the left edge, followed by three left-aligned text columns starting at about 7.8%, 38.9% and 69.9% of the width, each with a teal heading and bullets; a teal metrics band sits centred across the middle, above a row of three full-height-band photographs spanning the width, then two footnotes and a copyright line at the bottom left and the page number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Three photographs in a row below the metrics band: (1) left, a hotel lobby with a sweeping staircase with open wooden treads, floor-to-ceiling windows on the right, a bar with stools and a seating area of dark leather armchairs and wooden side tables, a wall of textured white three-dimensional panels on the left, ceiling downlights, warm neutral lighting, cropped to a rectangle about 29.8% wide and 35% high; (2) centre, an outdoor rooftop pool with a long rectangular pool of blue water edged with blue mosaic tile, a shaded cabana with dark wood slatted screens and white curtains, grey lounge chairs, a white umbrella and a city skyline in haze behind, daylight with a blue sky and white clouds, cropped to a rectangle about 39.4% wide and 35% high; (3) right, an evening patio with a red woven basket-style lounge chair in the foreground, a round dark fire pit with a visible flame, a stone and wood bench wall, dark dining chairs and a table, uplit trees and warm lamps, dusk blue sky, cropped to a rectangle about 30% wide and 35% high. The three photos are butted together with small white gaps and are not overlaid. A teal rectangle with a faint drop shadow overlays the top edge of the centre photo and the top strip of the other two. Metrics band: a solid teal rectangle with a faint soft shadow on its right and bottom edges, containing three large white numerals separated by two thin white vertical bars, with white captions beneath each numeral, each caption carrying a superscript footnote marker.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background #FFFFFF. Navigation tabs are mid-grey #AFAFAC with white uppercase Quicksand Medium text, letter-spaced, two lines each, and the active tab is teal #407676 with the same white text. Title is black #000000 in Quicksand Light, about 4.4% of slide height. Column headings are teal #407676 in Source Sans Pro SemiBold, about 3.3% of slide height. Bullet body text is dark grey #292929 in Source Sans Pro Regular, about 2.0% of slide height, with teal #407676 triangular bullet glyphs and a teal dash for the sub-bullet. Metrics numerals are white Source Sans Pro Black, about 5.2% of slide height, with white Source Sans Pro Regular captions about 2.0%. Footnotes are black Source Sans Pro Light about 1.2%, copyright likewise, page number grey #898989 Source Sans Pro Light about 1.7%. Accent colour is teal #407676. Band has square corners and a soft shadow. No gradients.

Comprehensive Renovation Scorecard
Host leveraged its unique relationship with Marriott to devise the Marriott Transformational Capital Program
(“MTCP”), a first-of-its-kind capex reinvestment program that included 15 properties. Outside of MTCP, 8 other
properties were subsequently added, bringing the total to 23 comprehensive renovations from 2018 to 2023.
21 of the completed properties have stabilized post-renovation with their average RevPAR Index share gain well
above the targeted range.

**Layout**

Six-tab navigation bar runs across the full top edge, with the second tab (RECENT HIGHLIGHTS) filled teal as the active section. The title sits left-aligned at about 7.9% from the left edge, followed by a full-width intro paragraph; below it a left column (about 7% to 25% of width) holds the TARGET and RESULT stat blocks, and a right-hand table spans about 28% to 95% of width. Footnotes and copyright sit bottom-left, with the page number bottom-right at about 95%; left margin about 7%, right margin about 5%. No logo and no slide footer band.

**Visuals**

Two stat blocks and one table; no photograph, chart, logo or icon. Left stat block 1: label TARGET in teal, large figure 3–5 in heavy teal, unit POINTS in light teal, caption ‘Targeted RevPAR Index Share Gain Post Renovation’ with superscript (2) in grey. Left stat block 2: label RESULT in teal, large figure +8.7 in heavy teal, unit POINTS in light teal, caption ‘Average RevPAR Index Share Gain for 21 Stabilized Properties’ in grey. Table: 3 columns and 8 rows of data beneath a two-part header. Header cell spanning columns 1 and 2 reads 15 MTCP ASSETS(1) on teal #407676; header cell over column 3 reads 8 ADDITIONAL ASSETS(1) on dark #203B3B. Column 1 rows: Coronado Island Marriott; New York Marriott Downtown; San Francisco Marriott Marquis; Santa Clara Marriott; San Antonio River Center Marriott; Minneapolis Marriott City Center; JW Marriott Buckhead; Ritz-Carlton Amelia Island. Column 2 rows: New York Marriott Marquis; Orlando World Center Marriott; Houston Medical Center Marriott; Marina Del Rey Marriott; Boston Copley Marriott; JW Marriott Houston; San Diego Marriott Marquis; cell empty. Column 3 rows: The Don CeSar; Hyatt Regency Maui; Westin Georgetown; Miami Marriott Biscayne Bay; Westin Denver Downtown; Fairmont Kea Lani; Hyatt Regency Coconut Point; Ritz-Carlton Naples. Bold marks stabilized properties per footnote 1; the last two rows of column 3 are regular weight. Row fills alternate #CED6D6 and #E8ECEC; no highlighted points.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white corporate slide with no decoration. Title in Quicksand Light, black, about 4.1% of slide height, sentence case. Intro body in Source Sans Pro Light, #292929, about 2.5% of slide height; key sentence has bold runs (Source Sans Pro Bold/Black). Accent teal #407676 for TARGET, 3–5, RESULT, +8.7 and table header; light teal #7FBABA for POINTS; grey #595959 for captions; table body text Source Sans Pro Bold #292929 at about 2.0% of slide height. Navigation tabs: Quicksand Medium, white on grey #AFAFAC, active tab teal #407676, uppercase, about 1.7% of slide height, letter-spaced. Table cells separated by thin white gutters, square corners, no shadows, no gradients. Footnotes and copyright are small Source Sans Pro Light at 1.2% of slide height. Page number grey #898989.

Hyatt Transformational Capital Program Overview
WHAT
Following the success of stabilized comprehensive renovations, Host has reached an agreement with Hyatt on the
Hyatt Transformational Capital Program (“HTCP”), a similar capex reinvestment program at six properties.
WHY

investments will position the hotels to compete better in their respective markets while seeking to enhance long-
term performance.
GOAL

combination of enhanced owner’s priority returns and RevPAR Index share gains.

**Layout**

Full-width slide with a six-tab section navigation bar across the top edge (tabs about 4.7% of slide height, edge to edge, the second tab highlighted). Title sits left-aligned at about 7.9% x and 8.7% y, followed by a stacked WHAT / WHY / GOAL block with labels in a left column and body text in a right column starting at about 17.7% x. A full-width light grey band holds three centred stat columns, and a full-width-margin table sits below it spanning about 9.6% to 90.4% x. Copyright line bottom-left and page number bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Table: three columns (HTCP ASSETS; RENOVATION START; TARGETED COMPLETION) and six data rows. Rows: Grand Hyatt Atlanta in Buckhead | Q1 2024 | Q1 2025 – Complete; Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill | Q1 2025 | Q3 2025 – Complete; Hyatt Regency Austin | Q2 2025 | Q4 2025 – Complete; Hyatt Regency Reston | Q4 2024 | Q1 2026 – Complete; Grand Hyatt Washington, DC | Q1 2024 | Q2 2026 - Complete; Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego | Q1 2025 | Q1 2027. Header row dark teal-navy #203B3B with white bold caps; body rows alternate #CED6D6 and #E8ECEC; cell text centred in columns 2 and 3, left-aligned in column 1. Three large numeric stat callouts ($525-550, $40, $125-200 million) in teal, each with a caption beneath; no chart. No photographs, logos or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background with a light grey #F2F2F2 band behind the stat row. Title in light sans-serif (Quicksand Light style), near-black #000000, large relative to body. Section labels WHAT, WHY, GOAL in semibold sans-serif teal #407676. Body text in Source Sans Pro Light, dark grey #292929 (some lines #000000), about 2.2% of slide height. Stat numerals in Source Sans Pro Black teal #407676, about 8.2% of slide height. Sub-labels MILLION in semibold light teal #7FBABA. Captions in Source Sans Pro Regular grey #595959. Navigation tabs in Quicksand Medium caps, white on grey #AFAFAC, active tab teal #407676. Table header #203B3B with white semibold caps. Square corners and no shadows, no gradients, thin white gaps between tabs and table cells.

Marriott Transformational Capital Program 2 Overview
WHAT
Following the success of stabilized comprehensive renovations, Host has reached a second agreement with Marriott on the Marriott Transformational Capital Program 2 (“MTCP2”), a similar capex reinvestment program at four additional properties.
WHY
Building on the success of prior Transformational Capital Programs, Host believes these portfolio investments will position the hotels to compete better in their respective markets while seeking to enhance long-term performance.
GOAL
Targeting mid-teens stabilized annual cash-on-cash returns through a combination of RevPAR Index share gains and enhanced owner’s priority returns. Similar to the first MTCP program, these targeted returns assume 3-to-5 points of RevPAR Index share gains at stabilization.
$300-350

**Layout**

**Text**

COMPANY OVERVIEW / RECENT HIGHLIGHTS / PORTFOLIO UPDATE / GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES / CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY / RECONCILIATIONS & SUPPLEMENTAL INFO / HOST / HOTELS & RESORTS® / Portfolio / Update / GRAND HYATT WASHINGTON

**Layout**

Full-width navigation bar of six equal-width tabs (about 16.7% wide, 4.6% tall, thin white gaps) runs across the top edge. Below it, a full-height photograph fills the left 61% of the slide, bleeding to the left, bottom and top-of-content edges. The right 39% is a plain white panel with the logo centred near the top of the panel (about 17% to 29% of height) and the title centred below it (about 39% to 53%). A translucent navy band runs across the bottom 6.8% of the slide, with the photo caption left-aligned at a 3% margin. There is no footer text and no slide number.

**Visuals**

Photograph: interior of a restaurant. Subject: a circular feature ceiling of tubular amber and bronze glass rods hung in tiers, with dark bronze elliptical rings; below it, teal curved upholstered banquette sofas and grey-beige upholstered armchairs with dark wood legs around round white-topped tables with dark pedestal bases, set with brown napkins, plates, glass tumblers and blue votive candles. Potted plants in stone planters (a fiddle-leaf fig and a snake plant) stand in the foreground; blue-to-white ombre curtains and copper-banded columns sit in the background. Composition: wide-angle, eye level, cropped at the left, right and top edges; the photo runs under the navy band at the bottom. Lighting: warm ambient light from the ceiling, soft and even. Dominant colours: amber/bronze, teal, beige, with some dark brown and green. The photo is boxed to its rectangle, not full-bleed, with no overlay on the image itself other than the navy band at its base. Logo: HOST HOTELS & RESORTS® corporate logo, centred in the white panel; a stylised mark of a gold block and a navy block above the wordmark HOST in navy serif capitals, with HOTELS & RESORTS® in smaller navy serif capitals beneath.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate look on a white slide. Navigation tabs are flat mid-grey tabs with white uppercase text, with the active section tab in purple. Title is a large light geometric sans in navy. Caption is small white uppercase sans on navy. Titles: navy #172645, about 5.9% of slide height. Body and nav text: white #FFFFFF, about 1.7% of slide height for the tabs and 1.5% for the caption. Typefaces: Quicksand (geometric sans, Medium for nav, Light for title) and Source Sans Pro Regular for the caption. Accents: purple #7567BD for the active tab, gold and navy in the logo. Shapes are flat rectangles with square corners, no borders, no shadows and no gradients. Navy band has 80% opacity.

### Slide 22

**Review notes**

- Worth studying: Quarterly growth rates are set in a compact bar-and-label layout beside a revenue-mix graphic, which makes the rate-driven story clear at a glance.
- Review: Slide 22 shows the chart problems: bars without a clear message, a pie chart with no labels on the slices, and a lot of empty space.
- Suggested repair: Replace the topic titles with conclusion titles, enlarge or cut the text and chart labels on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41, and label the pie slices directly on slide 22.

**Layout**

Full-width white slide with a six-tab section navigation bar across the top edge, title left-aligned at about 7.9% from the left, and a two-part body: a full-width clustered column chart with a pie chart and text block in the lower half. The subtitle paragraph spans the width below the title. A footnote sits above the footer line, with the copyright bottom-left and the page number bottom-right at about 95.3% from the left.

**Visuals**

Chart 1: clustered column chart titled '2026 Total RevPAR & RevPAR Growth vs. 2025' with superscript (1), subtitle 'Full Year 2026 Comparable Hotel Portfolio'. Two series: TRevPAR in purple #7567BD and RevPAR in navy #172645. No y-axis or gridlines are printed; the horizontal baseline is light grey. Categories left to right: Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026, FY 2026E. Labelled values TRevPAR / RevPAR: Q1 2026 4.6% / 4.4%; Q2 2026 5.8% / 6.9%; Q3 2026 7.3% / 8.8%; FY 2026E 6.0% / 6.75%. Bar heights are proportional to the printed values, with the Q3 RevPAR bar (8.8%) the tallest. No points are highlighted. Legend at top left: purple square labelled TRevPAR and navy square labelled RevPAR. Chart 2: pie chart titled '2025 & 2026E Revenue', a full circle with a navy slice (Room, about 60%, the larger slice, occupying the left and lower area) and a purple slice (F&B & Other, about 40%, upper right, starting at 12 o'clock and running clockwise). Thin white separator line between slices. Legend to the right of the pie: navy square 'Room – ~60%' and purple square 'F&B & Other – ~40%'. No tint, shadow or photograph.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Plain white background with no gradient, texture or shadow. Navigation tabs are flat grey #AFAFAC with white text, except the active tab PORTFOLIO UPDATE which is purple #7567BD. Title in light geometric sans (Quicksand Light), black #000000, about 4.1% of slide height (about 6.5% cap height relative). Subtitle and body in Source Sans Pro Light, dark grey #292929, about 2.6% of slide height. Chart headings in Source Sans Pro Black, #292929, about 2.6%. Chart subtitle italic Source Sans Pro, #595959, about 2.0%. Data labels Source Sans Pro Light, #404040, about 2.0%. Category labels Source Sans Pro Light, #595959, about 2.0%. Accents: purple #7567BD and navy #172645. Bars and pie are flat, square-cornered, with no outlines. Baseline light grey rule about 0.1% thick. Footnote text Source Sans Pro Light 1.2% in black; page number Source Sans Pro Light 1.7% in #898989.

**Visuals**

Photograph: a four- to five-storey resort hotel building with cream and beige stucco walls, dark brown hipped roof edges, and a prominent arched window with a grey-blue glazed frame on the central tower. Tall rectangular windows with blue-tinted glass and small wrought-iron balconies are spread across the facade. In the foreground is a long outdoor swimming pool with a blue mosaic tile edge and a light cream paving deck. Along the deck are grey-blue sun loungers and folded and open white and navy-blue patio umbrellas, with several palm trees and a pair of decorative lamp posts. A small sign reading NO DIVING is visible near the pool edge. Clear blue sky fills the upper left. The lighting is bright, even daylight with crisp shadows. The dominant colours are sky blue #4BA8E8, cream #E8DCC8, pool blue #2F7FB8 and navy #1F3A5F. The photograph is a rectangular box, cropped at the right edge at x 61.4% and at the bottom edge, not full-bleed on the right; it has no border. A navy band at 80% opacity overlays the bottom of the photo and extends across the full width. Logo: HOST HOTELS & RESORTS logo centred in the right column, consisting of a stylised square-cut emblem in gold #B39B63 and navy #172645 above the wordmark HOST in navy serif capitals with HOTELS & RESORTS® beneath in smaller navy serif capitals.

**Layout**

A full-width row of six equal navigation tabs runs across the top edge (0 to 4.7% of height), with the Growth tab highlighted in blue. The left-aligned title sits at x 7.9%, y 8.6%, followed by a left-aligned two-line subtitle and a blue sub-headline. The timeline is a horizontal bar of six equal year cells across the middle (y 53.5 to 58.8%), with creative projects above it and offensive additions below it, all in a left margin of about 8% and a right margin of about 2%. A navy callout sits bottom left, a footnote and copyright line run along the bottom, and the page number sits bottom right.

**Visuals**

Timeline diagram with a horizontal grey year bar divided into six equal cells labelled 2013, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, left to right. Above the bar, five light-blue ring markers (circles about 1.3% of slide width, light-blue fill with white centre dot) sit at the top of thin vertical connector lines that drop to the bar: 2013 (x about 8.0%), 2018 (x about 24.9%), 2020 (x about 41.4%), 2021 (x about 57.8%) and 2023 (x about 91.3%); each marker has a text block to its right describing a creative project. Below the bar, navy ring markers (navy fill with white centre dot) sit at the lower ends of thin navy connector lines: 2018 (y about 77.8%), 2021 (two markers, y about 68.1% and about 80.8%), 2022 (y about 75.1%) and 2023 (y about 84.5%); each marker has a text block beside it describing an offensive addition. A legend at the far left has a light-blue ring labelled CREATIVE PROJECTS and a navy ring labelled OFFENSIVE ADDITIONS, both as rotated vertical labels. Creative-project amounts appear in bold. Footnote marker (1) appears as superscript after underwriting. Below the timeline, a navy rectangular callout with a soft drop shadow carries the white text Offensive Additions target low-to-mid-teens cash-on-cash returns. No photographs or logos are present.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background with a flat, minimal corporate look. Navigation tabs are grey #AFAFAC, #A6A6A6 and #AFAFAC with the active Growth tab in blue #5DA6E0, and tab labels in white capitals. Title text is black #000000 in a light geometric sans (Quicksand Light), about 4.1% of slide height. Body text is black #000000 in Source Sans Pro, Light for descriptions, SemiBold for headings in capitals, and Black for dollar figures, at about 1.8% of slide height. The subtitle is Source Sans Pro Light about 2.6%. The blue sub-headline is Source Sans Pro SemiBold in #5DA6E0. Year bar is #747F81 with white Source Sans Pro Black numerals at about 3.3% of slide height. Accent colours are light blue #5DA6E0 and navy #172645. Shapes are square-cornered with no gradients; the callout has a soft drop shadow. Connector lines are thin 1 px strokes in grey and navy.

**Review notes**

- Review: Weaknesses are consequential: most content slides use titles that name a topic rather than a conclusion (6, 7, 10, 26, 28), tiny footnotes and dense text on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41 are hard to read, and the last 25 pages are reconciliation tables and legal text that cannot be read as a presentation.
- Suggested repair: Replace the topic titles with conclusion titles, enlarge or cut the text and chart labels on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41, and label the pie slices directly on slide 22.

**Layout**

Six equal navigation tabs run across the top edge (0 to 4.7% of height), the fourth tab (GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES) highlighted blue. The title sits left-aligned at x 7.9% under the tab bar, with a two-line intro paragraph and a blue subhead below it. The main area is a horizontal timeline: a full-width grey band at y 53.5% to 58.8% divided into four year segments (2024, 2025, 2026, ONGOING, the last one wider), with creative projects above the band and offensive additions below it, a navy callout bottom-left, a copyright line bottom-left and the page number bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Horizontal timeline diagram with four grey (#747F81) year segments in a band across the slide. Above the band (Creative Projects, light-blue markers #5DA6E0): a thin vertical line from a dot above the 2024 segment down to the band (NY Marriott Marquis Co-Generation Plant); a thin grey vertical line from a dot in the 2025 segment up to the text block (The Camby Seller Financing $13M); a light-blue dot at the top of the ONGOING panel (Washington Marriott Metro Center Seller Financing $114M). Below the band (Offensive Additions, navy #172645 markers): a thin grey line from the 2025 segment down to a navy dot at y 78.6% (Don Cesar Meeting Space Expansion & Enhanced Resiliency); a thin navy line from the 2026 segment down to a navy dot at y 75.3% (Villas at the Phoenician Canyon Suites); a navy ring dot at the top of the lower ONGOING panel (Four Seasons Orlando Condo Development). Two left-edge markers on the vertical labels: a light-blue dot at y about 48.5% beside CREATIVE PROJECTS and a navy ring at y about 60.5% beside OFFENSIVE ADDITIONS. Two pale lavender-blue panels (#E0E6F5) sit in the ONGOING column, one above the band (y 34.9% to 53.4%) and one below it (y 58.8% to 77.4%), each with a soft grey drop shadow and no border. The navy callout box (#172645) at bottom-left has a soft drop shadow. No photographs, logos or icons.

**Layout**

White slide with a full-width six-tile navigation bar across the top edge, the title left-aligned at about 8% from the left margin below it, then a two-line intro paragraph, a row of four large stat figures on the left and one on the right separated by vertical navy rules, and a full-width data table with footnotes, copyright line at bottom left and page number 28 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

One data table, no charts or photographs. Columns: row label, 2021 Actual, 2022 Actual, 2023 Actual, 2024 Actual, 2025 Actual, 2026 Full Year Forecast Low, 2026 Full Year Forecast High. Header row 1 reads Capital Expenditure by Type with 2021 to 2025 and a merged 2026 Full Year Forecast header. Header row 2 reads ($ in millions) with Actual under each year and Low and High. Body rows: ROI – MTCP, HTCP, & MTCP2(1): $126, $88, $51, $155, $191, $180, $195. ROI – All Other Projects: $167, $219, $144, $105, $91, $75, $85. Total ROI Investment (bold): $293, $307, $195, $260, $282, $255, $280. Renewals & Replacement (R&R): $134, $185, $274, $252, $287, $285, $305. Total ROI and R&R (bold): $427, $492, $469, $512, $569, $540, $585. R&R – Property Damage Reconstruction: -, $12, $177, $36, $75, $10, $15. Total Capital Expenditures (bold): $427, $504, $646, $548, $644, $550, $600. After a gap, Inventory Spend for Condo Development(2): -, -, $15, $64, $88, $17, $17. Total Capital Allocation: $427, $504, $661, $612, $732, $567, $617. No chart, legend or highlighted points. Also four large stat figures in blue (2,190 guest rooms completed renovations in 2025; 433K SF of meeting space; 109K SF of public space) and 8% (resiliency capex investment, average over past 6 years). No photographs, logos or icons.

**Design**

Background white #FFFFFF. Navigation tiles are flat grey #AFAFAC and #A6A6A6 with the active GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES tile in light blue #5DA6E0, all with white uppercase text. Title CapEx Investment Summary is black #000000 in a light geometric sans (Quicksand Light) at about 4.1% of slide height. Intro paragraph is #292929 in Source Sans Pro Light with the bold phrase in Source Sans Pro Black, about 2.6% of slide height. Stat numbers are light blue #5DA6E0 in Source Sans Pro Black at about 5.9% of slide height. Stat labels are grey #7F7F7F in Source Sans Pro SemiBold uppercase at about 2.0%. Left and right stat headings are navy #172645 Source Sans Pro Black uppercase at about 2.2%. Vertical rules are navy #172645. Table header rows are #5DA6E0 with white SemiBold text at about 2.0%; body text black #000000 Source Sans Pro Regular at about 2.0%, bold for totals. Body rows alternate white and #F2F2F2 with grey horizontal rules. Footnotes and copyright are Source Sans Pro Light about 1.2% in black; page number Source Sans Pro Light about 1.7% in #898989. No shadows, gradients, rounded corners or photographs.

COMPANY OVERVIEW / RECENT HIGHLIGHTS / PORTFOLIO UPDATE / GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES / CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY / RECONCILIATIONS & SUPPLEMENTAL INFO / Repositioning CapEx Case Study / THE SINGER OCEANFRONT RESORT / GOAL / Generate a double-digit cash-on-cash return through a tailored renovation to a lifestyle resort, including creating new profit-generating F&B outlets / WHAT WE DID / ► Repositioning renovations began in July 2023 and completed in June 2024 / ► Scope of renovations included: guestrooms/suites including extensive bathroom renovation; new and re-configured meeting space; extensive public space and F&B outlet renovations with new marketplace; expanded pool deck with gas firepits; exterior façade / LATEST RESULTS(1) / ► RevPAR index(2) share gain of 8.4 points (115.5 pre-renovation 3-year avg. vs. 123.9 for Q3 2026 TTM) / Q3 2026 TTM growth vs. Q2 2023 TTM: / ► TRevPAR +24% driven by increased group occupancy and F&B revenue / ► F&B revenue +74% driven by outlets / ► Resort able to attract higher quality groups, leading to +148% group revenue increase including doubling group room nights / BEFORE / AFTER / BEFORE / AFTER / 1) These results are illustrative only and there can be no guarantees that other projects will result in similar results. **Layout**

### Slide 31

**Text**

COMPANY OVERVIEW RECENT HIGHLIGHTS PORTFOLIO UPDATE GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY RECONCILIATIONS & SUPPLEMENTAL INFO / ROI Development Case Study / THE PHOENICIAN, A LUXURY COLLECTION RESORT / Nestled in the foothills of majestic Camelback Mountain, The Villas at Canyon Suites exemplify unparalleled luxury and contemporary sophistication. An exclusive addition to The Canyon Suites at The Phoenician, the AAA Five Diamond, Forbes Five Star resort-within-a-resort, this intimate enclave blends the serenity of home with uncompromising service and exceptional amenities. / © Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. / 31

**Layout**

Six equal-width navigation tabs run across the top edge in a single row, each spanning one sixth of the slide width at full slide height of 4.7 percent with two-line uppercase centred labels; below them a full-width photograph fills the band from 5.1 to 72.3 percent of the height. The title block is left-aligned at 7.8 percent from the left edge, with the title at 76.3 percent, subtitle at 80.7 percent and a three-line body paragraph from 86.0 to 93.4 percent; the copyright line sits at bottom left (6.9 percent) and the page number at bottom right (95.3 percent), both at about 96 percent of the height.

**Visuals**

Aerial photograph of The Phoenician resort in Scottsdale, Arizona, occupying the full slide width between the navigation bar and the title block. Subject: a low-rise, tan stucco and terracotta-roofed resort complex with flat-roofed villas, a blue-tinted circular pool with loungers and a small palm, a large man-made pond with a fountain at right, and manicured golf fairways and a sand bunker at left and bottom. Behind the resort rise brown, rocky, scrub-covered slopes of Camelback Mountain at left, a dense green urban and golf landscape to the right and distant blue-grey mountain ranges under pale blue sky. Composition: elevated three-quarter aerial view looking down and across the complex, with the mountain filling the upper left and the golf fairway filling the lower foreground. Lighting: bright, clear daylight with soft shadows. Dominant colours: tan and beige buildings, saturated green turf, brown and ochre hillside, pale blue sky and blue water. The photograph is rectangular, not cropped, not full-bleed, and carries no overlay or tint. Navigation tabs are flat grey rectangles with the active GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES tab in blue; no logos or icons appear.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white slide with a grey and blue top navigation bar of flat rectangles separated by thin white gaps; the title is in light grey-black geometric sans with a heavy black sans subtitle and a light sans body paragraph, all in black. Accent colour is the blue #5DA6E0 on the active tab. Navigation labels are white uppercase Quicksand Medium with wide letter spacing. Title is Quicksand Light at about 3.3 percent of slide height, subtitle is Source Sans Pro Black at about 3.3 percent, body is Source Sans Pro Light at about 2.0 percent, and footer and page number are Source Sans Pro Light at about 1.2 to 1.7 percent. Shapes have square corners, no borders, no shadows and no gradients.

### Slide 32

**Text**

COMPANY / OVERVIEW / RECENT / HIGHLIGHTS / PORTFOLIO / UPDATE / GROWTH / OPPORTUNITIES / CORPORATE / RESPONSIBILITY / RECONCILIATIONS & / SUPPLEMENTAL INFO / ROI Development Case Study / THE PHOENICIAN, A LUXURY COLLECTION RESORT / GOAL / Generate a double-digit cash-on-cash return on vacant land / adjacent to the Canyon Suites, a resort-within-a-resort / Offer a new luxury residential product at the Canyon Suites / to capture demand from families, executives, golf groups, / entertainment, pro sports teams, and other VIPs / Benefit from overflow demand from the Phoenician / Residences / BEFORE / AFTER / ROI DEVELOPMENT / Construction of 8 luxury villas at the Canyon Suites: / 20 additional keys consisting of 4 two-bedroom, 2 / three-bedroom, and 2 four-bedroom suites / All suites include outdoor firepits; three- and four- / bedroom suites also include hot tubs / Private swimming pool including a hot tub, four / private cabanas, poolside dining, and firepit seating / ADDITIONAL FEATURES / Villas include full kitchens and wet bars; / guests may opt to pre- and re-stock F&B / during their stay / Gas fireplaces in all living rooms / Seamless fusion of indoor and outdoor / spaces with stacking glass doors / Golf course and mountain views / In-suite washer and dryer / Private villa golf carts with designated / parking / AFTER / BEFORE / © Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. / 32

**Layout**

Two-zone layout: a full-height photo collage fills the left side and is cut on a diagonal from roughly x 33% at the top edge to x 65% at the bottom, leaving a white right panel holding the title, subtitle and three text sections. A six-tab grey navigation bar runs across the top edge at full width, with the Growth Opportunities tab highlighted in blue. The title is centred in the right panel; section headings and bullets are left-aligned from about x 51% to 68%. The copyright line and page number sit in the bottom-right corner with a margin of about 4% from the right edge.

**Visuals**

Photo collage (one composite image, 1112 by 1215 pixels, placed at x 0 y 4.5 w 65.7 h 95.5 percent) made of five interior photographs of a luxury villa. Top panel: a living room with a grey sectional sofa, patterned rug, round dark coffee table with flowers and books, a stone-clad wall with a wall-mounted TV, and an open kitchen with wood cabinets in the background; warm daylight and neutral grey, beige and wood tones. Middle left: a bathroom with a freestanding white tub, a double wood vanity with a white countertop and arched mirror, and stacked white towels; cool grey marble walls. Middle centre: a living room opening onto a terrace with stacking glass doors, a pond and golf course view, grey sofa and armchairs, and a stone fireplace wall; blue sky and green landscape visible. Bottom left: a bedroom with a king bed with white linens, a patterned rug, a view through sliding glass doors to a patio, and a floor lamp; neutral beige tones. Bottom right: a dining area and kitchen with a long dark wood table, upholstered chairs, pendant lights and wood cabinetry; neutral tones. The photos are full-colour, uncropped at their edges, with no overlay or tint, and are cut by the white diagonal wedge on the right. Icons (outline style, blue #5DA6E0, about 4 to 5 percent of slide width): target with arrow at about x 45.3 y 21.3 w 4.3 h 5.7 next to GOAL; a checkmark with three horizontal lines at about x 51.3 y 45.3 w 4.9 h 4.5 next to ROI DEVELOPMENT; a ruler at about x 59.6 y 67.2 w 5.2 h 6.8 next to ADDITIONAL FEATURES. Navigation tabs are plain rectangles, not icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, with the photo collage placed over the left side. Clean corporate look with a white background and a grey navigation bar. Navigation tabs use Quicksand Medium capitals in white, centred, two lines per tab; inactive tab fill #AFAFAC or #A6A6A6, active tab fill #5DA6E0. Slide title ROI Development Case Study is Quicksand Light in black #000000, sentence case, about 4.1 percent of slide height (lowercase size). Subtitle THE PHOENICIAN, A LUXURY COLLECTION RESORT is Source Sans Pro Black capitals in #292929, about 2.6 percent of slide height. Section headings GOAL, ROI DEVELOPMENT and ADDITIONAL FEATURES are Source Sans Pro Black capitals in blue #5DA6E0, about 2.0 percent of slide height. Body text is Source Sans Pro Light in #292929, about 2.0 percent of slide height, with generous line spacing of about 2.4 percent of slide height between lines. Bullets are blue #5DA6E0 right-pointing triangle glyphs. Copyright line is Source Sans Pro Light, about 1.2 percent. Page number is Source Sans Pro Light in grey #898989, about 1.7 percent. No shadows, gradients, rounded corners or borders; the only line-like feature is the diagonal photo edge.

**Layout**

Six equal-width navigation tabs run across the top edge of the slide, flush to the top with no margin, the fourth tab (GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES) highlighted. Below them the title sits left-aligned at about 8% from the left edge. The body is two columns: a narrow left column (about 4% to 24%) holding a centred heading, three icon-and-caption pairs, and a right column (about 29% to 96%) holding two stacked case studies, each with a blue heading, a photo at left and text at right, separated by a thin horizontal rule at about 54% height. A thin vertical rule at about 26% separates the columns. The copyright footer sits bottom-left at about 7% from the left and the page number bottom-right at about 95%.

**Visuals**

Three line icons in the left column, all drawn in navy #172645 with a thin uniform stroke and no fill: (1) a wave breaking over three horizontal wavy lines, about 10% to 16% horizontal, 36% to 42% vertical, above the caption about flooding; (2) a stylised flame outline, about 11% to 15% horizontal, 54% to 61% vertical, above the fire-break caption; (3) a high-voltage electricity pylon in outline with a cross-braced lattice and crossarms, about 11% to 15% horizontal, 73% to 80% vertical, above the power caption. Two photographs in the right column, both full-colour, rectangular, boxed with sharp corners, no overlay or tint. Photo 1 (The Don CeSar, 640 by 395 px): an aerial view of a pink Mediterranean-style hotel with a white-capped tower on the left, a turquoise pool with lounge chairs and green umbrellas in the centre, palm trees, a long sandy beach with rows of umbrellas, and calm blue-turquoise ocean across the upper right under a clear pale blue sky; daylight, bright even lighting, dominant colours pink, sand, turquoise and green; not cropped. Photo 2 (The Ritz-Carlton, Naples, 640 by 387 px): an aerial view of a tall tan/peach hotel tower with terracotta-tiled roofs and a lower wing, a pool with blue loungers and palms in the foreground, a parking lot at lower right, the Gulf beach and turquoise sea at upper left and a skyline of white high-rise condominiums at upper right under a blue sky; daylight, dominant colours peach, terracotta, turquoise and blue; not cropped.

**Visuals**

Photograph: aerial view of an oceanfront resort complex, the Ritz-Carlton O’Ahu, Turtle Bay. Two long hotel wings with cream-coloured facades and rows of balconies run diagonally, and their roofs and a central tower roof are covered with dark blue solar panels in rectangular arrays. Breaking waves and deep blue ocean fill the upper left, with a grassy headland and palm trees beyond the wings. Lower left shows a curved pool with white lounge chairs and cabanas, and a long blue lagoon pool at centre. Lawns are green. Daylight, bright and even, with a crisp shadow-free look. Composition is a high oblique aerial view, cropped at the left and bottom edges and not full-bleed; it is boxed by the nav bar above and the dark band below, and a dark navy band at 80% opacity overlaps its bottom 6.8%. Dominant colours: ocean blue, solar navy, cream white and grass green. Logo: HOST HOTELS & RESORTS logo, a stylised pair of abutting square shapes (one gold, one navy) above the navy serif wordmark HOST and the smaller navy caps line HOTELS & RESORTS with a registered mark. The logo is placed at about x 73.8 to 87.3, y 16.7 to 29.3, navy #172645 and gold #B39B5E.

**Layout**

A full-width row of six equal navigation tabs runs across the top edge (each about 16.7 percent wide and 4.7 percent high) with uppercase labels. The title sits left-aligned at x 7.9 percent, y 8.6 percent, followed by a left-aligned intro paragraph; a centred HIGHLIGHTS heading sits above a two-column grid of four centred section headings with bullet blocks beneath (left column from x 5.8 percent, right column from x 53 percent). Footnote lines sit at the bottom left and bottom right, with the copyright at bottom left and the page number 35 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

No photographs, charts, tables, logos or icons. The bottom 60 percent of the slide carries a gradient background image (720 by 322 pixels) fading from white at the top to pale green at the bottom edge. Along the top edge are six flat rectangular navigation tabs: five grey (#AFAFAC or #A6A6A6) and the fifth tab, CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY, filled green #62944D as the active tab. Tabs are butted together with thin white gaps and have square corners and no shadow.

**Review notes**

- Review: Weaknesses are consequential: most content slides use titles that name a topic rather than a conclusion (6, 7, 10, 26, 28), tiny footnotes and dense text on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41 are hard to read, and the last 25 pages are reconciliation tables and legal text that cannot be read as a presentation.
- Suggested repair: Replace the topic titles with conclusion titles, enlarge or cut the text and chart labels on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41, and label the pie slices directly on slide 22.

A full-width top navigation bar of six equal grey tabs runs across the top edge of the slide, with the fifth tab (CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY) highlighted green. Below it the title and subtitle are left-aligned at about 7.9% from the left edge, with a large table image spanning nearly the full width from 1% to 100% of the slide between roughly 24% and 89% of the height. Footnotes sit in two columns beneath the table, the copyright line sits bottom-left at about 6.9% and the page number bottom-right at about 95%.

**Visuals**

A single placed image (1116 by 547 pixels) containing a five-column table with small line icons in the first column. Columns: PRIORITIES, FOCUS AREAS, 2030 TARGETS, STATUS, 2025 PROGRESS*. Rows grouped by priority: Net Positive Environmental Impact (green-teal globe and leaf icon) has four rows: Decarbonization with 54% absolute reduction of Scope 1 and 2 emissions (from 2019 baseline), status ON TRACK with a teal bar about 60% filled and a thin tan trailing line, progress 36% reduction; Decarbonization with 50% of electricity use will be sourced from renewable sources, ON TRACK with teal bar about 65% filled, progress 30.6% from renewable sources; Water Stewardship with 25% reduction of water usage per occupied room in water-stressed areas (from 2019 baseline), status INITIATING in tan text with a grey line and no fill, progress 1.3% increase¹; Waste Reduction with 100% of major renovation projects divert at least 50% of waste by volume from landfill across at least three waste streams, ON TRACK with teal bar about 60% filled, progress 64.7% of projects diverted at least 50% waste. Climate Resilient Portfolio (green shield and building icon) has one row: LEED® Certifications, 40% of our consolidated hotels will achieve LEED® green building certification, ON TRACK with green bar about 70% filled, progress 30.4% of portfolio LEED® certified. Inclusive Workplace Culture (purple speech-bubble and people icon) has two rows: Employee Engagement, 85% or more of our employees are highly engaged each year, ON TRACK*** with a full-length purple bar, progress 92% highly engaged in most recent survey**; Inclusion and Belonging, Candidate slates for all externally sourced positions include qualified individuals with varying backgrounds and experiences², ON TRACK*** full purple bar, progress 100% included qualified candidates with varying backgrounds and experiences. Strategic Community Impact (blue hands and people icon) has one row: Community Impact, 90% or more of employees participate in charitable giving and/or volunteerism each year, ON TRACK*** full blue bar, progress 96% participation rate. Resilient Supply Chain (brown building and worker icon) has two rows: Responsible Sourcing, 100% of direct suppliers trained annually on Host’s responsible sourcing and human rights policies, ON TRACK*** brown bar about 70% filled, progress 54% of direct suppliers trained; Resilient Supply Chain, Supplier engagements for direct capital expenditures will target qualified suppliers, consultants and contractors that increase supply chain resilience, ON TRACK full brown bar, progress 16.4% of spend was with qualified suppliers³. Status bars are short horizontal bars with a thin tan line continuing to the right edge. Thin coloured rules separate the priority groups, and a thin grey rule sits under the header row. Footnotes ¹ to ⁴ and ** and *** are printed in tiny type in two columns beneath the table rows. No photographs or logos appear.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF covering the whole slide. White background with grey and green navigation tabs. Navigation labels are white, Quicksand Medium, all capitals, letter-spaced, about 1.7% of slide height, centred in two lines. Title '2030 Targets' is black Quicksand Light, sentence case, about 4.1% of slide height (roughly 3 times body size). Subtitle is dark grey #292929 Source Sans Pro Light at about 2.6% of slide height. Table text is dark grey #292929 in Quicksand Medium at roughly 1.5% to 1.8% of slide height, with bold numerals. Priority names are coloured per group: Net Positive teal #2A7F7A, Climate green #62944D, Inclusive Workplace purple #4E3670, Strategic Community blue #2B3FA0, Resilient Supply Chain brown #4A3F38. Column headers are small grey capitals #7F7F7F. Table rows alternate very faint warm-grey #F7F7F5 and white. Shapes are square-cornered with no shadows, no gradients, no rounded corners. Footer copyright is black Source Sans Pro at about 1.2% of slide height; page number is grey #898989 at about 1.7%.

**Review notes**

- Review: Weaknesses are consequential: most content slides use titles that name a topic rather than a conclusion (6, 7, 10, 26, 28), tiny footnotes and dense text on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41 are hard to read, and the last 25 pages are reconciliation tables and legal text that cannot be read as a presentation.
- Suggested repair: Replace the topic titles with conclusion titles, enlarge or cut the text and chart labels on slides 26-27, 37 and 40-41, and label the pie slices directly on slide 22.
